name: India–Pakistan
value: Indus treaty in abeyance; no LoC strike found
summary: India keeps the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance; troops fired at suspected movement near the LoC on 16 Nov
state: Indian troops fired about two dozen rounds at suspicious movement near the Line of Control in Poonch's Sawjian sector early on 16 Nov and began a search; no exchange with Pakistani forces was reported (PTI via Telangana Today). India continues to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance despite a September Court of Arbitration ruling that it remains in force (Dawn; JURIST). No cross-border strike or mobilisation was found as of 18 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Travellers should follow FCDO advice for India and Pakistan, which advises against travel near the Line of Control.
rubric_hit: Treaty suspension in force = Watch; no cross-border strikes

sources.title: Telangana Today (PTI) — Army opens fire after suspicious movement near LoC in J&K's Poonch
JURIST — Court of Arbitration rules Indus Waters Treaty remains in force

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
